claims.statement: For a finite reference dataset D of n observations, a finite metric and 2<=m<=n, core_m(p) is the mth ordered distance to observations in D, including p itself. N_m(p) retains every observation at distance at most that boundary, including all ties. The inspected exact linear scans and heap include the indexed query and boundary ties; a fixed-count truncation is not the same convention. The m range describes the well-defined distinct-point metric case, not a claim that every constructor enforces it.

claims.statement: For o in N_m(p), reach_m(p,o)=max(core_m(o),d(p,o)), using the neighbor radius. Set lrd_m(p)=|N_m(p)| divided by the sum of these reaches, and OF_m(p) to the mean of lrd_m(o)/lrd_m(p) over N_m(p). Thus self reachability is core_m(p), not zero, and the self term contributes a ratio of one when defined. The formulas require positive finite mean reaches for all densities used. These inverse-distance quantities are not normalized probability densities, and the resulting relative score is not an outlier probability or an automatic binary decision.

The inspected implementation first stores neighborhoods and core radii, then computes all local reachability densities, then averages their neighbor-to-query ratios. It does not run an OPTICS ordering or extract a clustering. Pairwise reachability in the score must not be replaced with a minimum reachability accumulated during an OPTICS traversal.

claims.statement: OPTICS-OF and original LOF are retained separately because including the query changes both density and score averaging. Under absolute distance, D={0,1,3} gives OPTICS-OF scores {1,1,3/2} at m=2, whereas self-excluded LOF gives {1,1,2} at k=1, despite identical core radii. At m=3, OPTICS-OF gives {1,1,1}, while LOF at k=2 gives {11/12,6/5,11/12}. These exact curator calculations rule out identifying the two procedures merely by shifting the neighbor-count parameter.

claims.statement: Boundary ties can change scores: for D={0,2,4,5} and m=2, point 2 has three retained neighbors and score 4/3; selecting only itself and neighbor 0 instead gives score 1. Positive uniform scaling of every distance cancels from defined density ratios, but feature-specific scaling can change neighborhoods. When m=n, every neighborhood is D and reach_m(p,o)=core_m(o), so all densities are equal and all defined scores are one. A score of one therefore does not by itself establish domain normality.

A fallback zero or nonfinite output outside the stated finite domain is not evidence of normality.

claims.statement: For n reference observations and 1<=k<=n-1, k-distance(p) is the kth ordered distance to other observations, excluding p itself. N_k(p) contains every other observation whose distance is at most that boundary, including all ties, so its size can exceed k. The reference dataset and dissimilarity define locality; the procedure does not require labeled normal/outlier examples or an explicit clustering.

evidence.locator: Section 4, Definitions 3-4, printed/PDF p3; Section 1, p1

claims.statement: Define reach_k(p,o)=max(k-distance(o),d(p,o)), using the neighbor o's radius, not p's. Reachability is generally asymmetric. Local reachability density lrd_k(p) is the reciprocal of the mean reachability over o in N_k(p), and LOF_k(p) is the mean of lrd_k(o)/lrd_k(p) over that same neighborhood. These formulas require nonempty neighborhoods and positive finite mean reaches for the densities used. Reachability density has inverse-distance units; it is not a normalized probability density. LOF is a dimensionless relative score.

A large score indicates lower reachability density relative to neighbors; it is neither an outlier probability nor a universal decision threshold. The paper's near-one bound assumes a closed two-hop neighborhood and bounded positive reachability variation. Scores can be below one: for D={0,1,3} under absolute distance and k=2, the scores are {11/12,6/5,11/12}. At k=1 they are {1,1,2}, reversing the center-versus-endpoint ordering. Two arbitrarily separated observations both score one at k=1; absolute isolation alone is not enough. These examples are exact curator calculations.

evidence.locator: Definition 7 and Lemma 1, printed/PDF p4; Sections 5-6, pp4-8; research/discovery/local-outlier-factor-boundaries.py

claims.statement: Boundary ties are part of the original definition: D={0,2,4,5}, k=1 gives point 2 score 3/2 when both equidistant neighbors are retained, but score 1 if an exact-k implementation chooses only neighbor 0. Coincident observations can give zero mean reachability and undefined density ratios; the paper assumes no duplicates and mentions a distinct-coordinate alternative without making an additive regularizer part of core LOF. Multiplying every distance by a positive constant leaves the unregularized core score unchanged when defined; feature-specific rescaling can change neighborhoods and scores. For D={0,1,3}, k=2, reach(0,1)=2 exceeds d(0,1)=1, so the paper's informal k=2 raw-distance reduction is not generally implied by its self-excluded definitions.

evidence.locator: Definitions 3-7 and duplicate discussion, printed/PDF pp3-4; Section 6, p7; exact curator calculations in research/discovery/local-outlier-factor-boundaries.py

claims.statement: Scores can vary nonmonotonically with k. The paper suggests choosing a lower and upper neighborhood size and ranking each point by its maximum LOF over that range; this is an optional multiscale ranking heuristic, distinct from a fixed-k score. Suggested lower bounds near 10 and common choices around 10-20 are empirical guidance, not mathematical validity constraints or universally optimal defaults. Small groups can appear ordinary relative to one another at some scales, so the chosen range affects which deviations are exposed.

The inspected scikit-learn 1.7.2-linked implementation uses a fixed neighbor count, excludes the indexed query for fitted training scores, and adds 1e-10 to mean reachability before inversion. It exposes negative LOF as negative_outlier_factor_; auto contamination chooses offset -1.5, while supplied contamination chooses a training-score percentile and labels scores strictly below it. These are implementation choices, not the paper's all-ties and unregularized definition or a universally validated 1.5 cutoff. Ties can prevent an exact requested outlier fraction. A fixed additive epsilon also prevents automatically transferring exact uniform-scale invariance.

native_identity_field_matches.name: PointNet++
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A hierarchical point-set neural architecture that repeatedly samples centroids, groups metric neighborhoods and applies local PointNet feature extraction, with multi-scale or multi-resolution constructions for variable sampling density.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Learning real-time A*
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A real-time heuristic learning algorithm that moves to a minimum estimated path-cost neighbor, stores that minimum edge-cost-plus-heuristic value at the state it leaves, and retains learned state estimates across repeated problem-solving trials with the same goals.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Real-time A*
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A real-time heuristic search algorithm that moves to a neighbor with minimum edge-cost-plus-heuristic estimate and stores the second-best such estimate at the state it leaves, using bounded lookahead or initial heuristics for previously unvisited states.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Neural autoregressive distribution estimator
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A fully visible autoregressive density model whose ordered variable conditionals are computed by neural networks that share input-to-hidden parameters and recursively reuse prefix computations.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Vicinal risk minimization
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A risk-minimization principle that chooses a predictor from a specified function class by minimizing expected loss under an estimated distribution built from training examples and their neighborhoods.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Triplet Markov field
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A latent-variable spatial-model family that introduces an auxiliary field so the complete hidden, auxiliary and observed triplet has a normalized Gibbs factorization on a specified neighborhood graph, while its hidden–observed projection need not remain Markov on that graph.

native_identity_field_matches.name: CLARANS clustering
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A randomized medoid-clustering algorithm that searches fixed-size sets of representative observations by accepting improving single swaps and restarting after a budget of unsuccessful neighbor trials.

native_identity_field_matches.name: UMAP
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A nonlinear embedding algorithm that constructs a locally scaled, symmetrized nearest-neighbor similarity graph and places its vertices in a lower-dimensional space using sampled attractive and repulsive updates.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Mean shift
native_identity_field_matches.definition: Mode-seeking clustering that moves candidate centers toward local density maxima.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Novelty SAT heuristic
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A clause-based SAT local-search heuristic that ranks candidate flips by total violation count with oldest-variable tie breaks, normally selects the best candidate, and sometimes selects the second-best when the best was the most recently flipped variable in that clause.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Tree-structured Parzen Estimator
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A sequential hyperparameter optimization method that separates observations by a loss quantile, fits tree-structured densities for the better and remaining configurations, and proposes evaluations using their density ratio as an expected-improvement ranking.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Adaptive rejection sampling
native_identity_field_matches.definition: The Gilks–Wild univariate rejection sampler that uses tangents to a concave log density as a piecewise-linear upper hull and chords as a lower hull, updating these bounds from evaluated proposals.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Prototype-based domain description
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A one-class decision rule that accepts a query when its metric distance to at least one prototype, plus that prototype's stored radius offset, is no greater than a common threshold.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Support vector data description
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A one-class support-estimation algorithm that learns a sphere in an input or kernel feature space by minimizing squared radius plus linearly penalized nonnegative distance-constraint violations, then accepts a query when its feature lies within or on the learned sphere.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Graph attention network
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A graph neural architecture that updates node representations using learned attention weights over graph neighborhoods.

native_identity_field_matches.name: HDBSCAN
native_identity_field_matches.definition: Hierarchical density-based clustering that selects clusters across density scales.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Metropolis–Hastings sampling
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that proposes a new state from a specified transition distribution and accepts it with the smaller of one and the target-density ratio multiplied by the reverse-to-forward proposal ratio, otherwise retaining the current state.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Fast Local Search
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A neighborhood-search procedure that uses activation bits to scan selected subneighborhoods, deactivating unsuccessful ones and reactivating those affected by accepted improvements.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Fast condensed prototype-based domain description
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A heuristic for selecting PDD prototypes that samples remaining reference observations, computes their radius offsets against the full dataset, accumulates eligible candidates, and greedily selects them by uncovered-reference gain with an adaptive sampling schedule.

native_identity_field_matches.name: GraphSAGE
native_identity_field_matches.definition: An inductive graph representation architecture that learns neighborhood aggregation functions to generate node embeddings from features.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Metropolis-adjusted Langevin algorithm
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A Metropolis–Hastings sampler that proposes a Gaussian step with drift proportional to the target log-density gradient and corrects the asymmetric proposal with an accept/reject test.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Laplacian Eigenmaps
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A spectral embedding algorithm that builds a weighted neighborhood graph and uses nonconstant generalized eigenvectors of its graph Laplacian to place strongly connected points close together.

native_identity_field_matches.name: R-Novelty SAT heuristic
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A Novelty-derived SAT heuristic whose choice between the best and second-best flips depends on their objective-score gap when the best variable was most recently flipped; its original 1997 search strategy also includes a periodic random clause-variable move.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Accelerated graph degree linkage
native_identity_field_matches.definition: An approximate graph degree linkage algorithm that selects merges from maintained cluster-neighbor sets and updates those sets locally instead of searching every current cluster pair.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Auto-exponential Markov random field
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A finite pairwise Markov-field model for nonnegative continuous site values with exponential full conditionals whose rates are positive baseline terms plus nonnegative symmetric linear neighbor interactions.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Condensed prototype-based domain description
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A greedy prototype-selection procedure that constructs kth-neighbor radius offsets from the full reference dataset and repeatedly chooses the prototype covering the most still-uncovered eligible reference locations under the PDD distance rule.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Isomap
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction algorithm that estimates manifold geodesic distances by shortest paths in a local neighborhood graph and applies classical multidimensional scaling to those estimated distances.

native_identity_field_matches.name: CHAMELEON clustering
native_identity_field_matches.definition: A graph-clustering procedure that first partitions a sparse neighbor graph into small subclusters and then agglomerates them using interconnectivity and closeness normalized by their internal bisection statistics.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Extended Guided Local Search
native_identity_field_matches.definition: The Tsang–Mills–Ford extension of Guided Local Search that combines cost-scaled penalty weighting, aspiration for a new best original-objective solution despite an augmented-objective penalty, and probabilistic random neighborhood moves.

native_identity_field_matches.name: Nearest-neighbor ratio data description
